note: Write the question, prediction, and interpretation rule before the test. Status 'proposed' means drafted, not adopted: only a named human may set 'registered'. A measurement must cite a registered entry and the fingerprint it was judged against, so a rule edited after the result is detectable.

preregistrations.title: Deploy-output timing on inert hardware
preregistrations.proposed_by: Automated assistant during the 2026-09-28 evidence review
preregistrations.question: When the firmware requests a 50 ms deploy delay, when does GPIO 33 rise relative to the trigger, and how much does that vary?
preregistrations.prediction: Edge at 50,000 us after the trigger reference; the paper claims jitter below 1,000 us. No model predicts the spread.

measured: time from trigger-reference edge to GPIO 33 rising edge, per trial

preregistrations.interpretation_rule: Report median, maximum absolute deviation from 50,000 us, and trial count. R-C2-JITTER is satisfied only if the maximum absolute deviation over at least 1,000 trials is below 1,000 us after subtracting the instrument's stated timing uncertainty. Fewer trials: report the observation, do not evaluate the requirement.
preregistrations.measurement_method: Logic analyzer or oscilloscope sampling at 1 MHz or faster on GPIO 33 and on a second GPIO toggled immediately before trigger_deployment_sequence(); both channels share the instrument's clock.
known_limitations: The trigger-reference toggle itself adds a small, unmeasured offset.
Bench conditions exclude flight vibration, temperature, and brownout.
preregistrations.safety: Inert only: nothing connected to GPIO 33 except the instrument; ignition servo mechanically disconnected; no energetic material present.

preregistrations.title: Torsion spring rate of the supplied spring
preregistrations.proposed_by: Automated assistant during the 2026-09-28 evidence review
preregistrations.question: What is the torque-angle rate of the spring that would be installed, and does it match the 220 N*m/rad in the claim?

measured: torque at each angle, loading and unloading

preregistrations.interpretation_rule: Fit torque against angle over the rated range; report slope with its standard error and the hysteresis. Compare with 220 N*m/rad; the acceptance tolerance must be written here by the registering human before testing.
preregistrations.measurement_method: Static torque-angle fixture with a calibrated torque gauge or load cell at a known lever arm.
known_limitations: Static rate only; dynamic and temperature effects are not captured.
preregistrations.safety: Stored-energy hazard: restrain the spring, wear eye protection, release slowly.

preregistrations.title: Stationary roll-estimate drift
preregistrations.proposed_by: Automated assistant during the 2026-09-28 evidence review
preregistrations.question: How far does the firmware roll estimate drift over 10 minutes with the rocket stationary and level, after CALIBRATE?
preregistrations.prediction: None. This is an exploratory characterization; no model predicts the drift.

measured: roll_deg from LOG rows (rocket clock) over 600 s
rate_deg_s from the same LOG rows, integrated over time offline
recorded: whether CALIBRATE was sent and when

preregistrations.interpretation_rule: Report the roll change over 600 s, the maximum excursion, and the integrated rate over the same window. Because no prediction exists, the result describes this unit only and sets a baseline; it cannot pass or fail.
preregistrations.measurement_method: Dashboard session with DUMPLOG every 10 s to capture rocket-clock LOG rows; audit with python -m evidence audit.
known_limitations: The ring buffer holds about 12 s; missed dumps leave gaps that must be reported, not interpolated.

In this pose the accelerometer holds roll_deg near its reference, so roll_deg alone cannot show gyro drift. Integrated rate_deg_s reads the gyro without that correction, and only it applies to gyro-only operation (D-027).
preregistrations.safety: Inert only: ignition servo disconnected; launcher left in SAFE.

preregistrations.title: Fuze S&A no-fire checks on inert hardware
preregistrations.proposed_by: Chief weapons engineer under the program sponsor's Phase 6.1 implementation order of 2026-11-15
preregistrations.question: Does the physical fuze S&A chain stay safe through drop, static-acceleration, and thermal-storage handling: 1.5 m drop onto each face, 8 g static for 5 s, and -40/+60 C soak?
preregistrations.prediction: SAFE throughout; no initiator continuity change. The software-in-the-loop harness (Firmware/sa_harness.py) passes the logic halves of these checks; the hardware halves are unmeasured.

measured: fuze state per the FUZE telemetry line

preregistrations.interpretation_rule: The 6.1.1 gate passes only if every trial leaves the fuze SAFE with unchanged initiator continuity. A single arming or continuity change fails the gate and stops the program.
preregistrations.measurement_method: Drop rig and static fixture with the fuze unit instrumented for the FUZE line; thermal chamber per MIL-STD-810 method 503 style.
known_limitations: Logic-level halves already validated by Firmware/tests/test_sa_harness.py; only the hardware response is new here.
preregistrations.safety: Inert fuze units only; no energetic material; initiator continuity measured with a safe ohmmeter.

preregistrations.title: Fuze S&A arm-in-order on inert hardware
preregistrations.proposed_by: Chief weapons engineer under the program sponsor's Phase 6.1 implementation order of 2026-11-15
preregistrations.question: Does each single arming event (launch acceleration alone, canard deployment alone, flight time alone) leave the fuze SAFE, and do all three in order arm it?
preregistrations.prediction: Each single event: SAFE. All three in order: ARMED, visible as FUZE,ARMED on the telemetry line within 60 s of the sequence completing.

measured: fuze state after each single event
fuze state after the full sequence

preregistrations.interpretation_rule: The 6.1.2 and 6.1.3 gates pass only if every single-event trial stays SAFE and every in-order trial arms. One failure of either fails the gate.
preregistrations.measurement_method: Bench driving of the flight computer per Firmware/sa_harness.py scenarios, with the real MPU6050 stimulated by the fixture and the fins-deployed latch driven by the deploy output.
known_limitations: Software-in-the-loop halves already pass in Firmware/tests/test_sa_harness.py.
preregistrations.safety: Inert fuze units; fire output into a lamp or scope, never an initiator.

preregistrations.title: Fuze impact function and PD delay on inert hardware
preregistrations.proposed_by: Chief weapons engineer under the program sponsor's Phase 6.1 implementation order of 2026-11-15
preregistrations.question: Does an armed fuze function on an 8 g+ impact deceleration, with the fire output rising after the selected PD delay (0/5/10/20 ms), and does a sub-threshold deceleration leave it armed?
preregistrations.prediction: FUNCTION on -20 g; fire output HIGH after the selected delay within +1 ms; no function on -5 g. The logic halves pass in Firmware/tests/test_sa_harness.py.

measured: fire-output edge time relative to the stimulus

preregistrations.interpretation_rule: The 6.1.4 gate passes only if every armed trial functions with the delay within +1 ms of selection and every sub-threshold trial stays armed.
preregistrations.measurement_method: Shaker or impulse fixture driving the MPU6050; the fire output on GPIO 32 measured with a scope at 1 MHz.
known_limitations: Impact stimulus shape differs from real impact; delay accuracy at the ms level is the quantity of interest.
preregistrations.safety: Inert fuze units; fire output into a lamp or scope, never an initiator.

preregistrations.title: Command-link security on the bench (replay, forgery, two-key)
preregistrations.proposed_by: Chief weapons engineer under the program sponsor's Phase 6.1 implementation order of 2026-11-15
preregistrations.question: Does the physical launcher reject replayed AUTH packets, forged HMACs, and single-key OVERRIDE attempts, and accept valid two-key OVERRIDE and authenticated commands?
preregistrations.prediction: All forgeries and replays rejected with CMD_REJECT rows logged; valid authenticated commands accepted; OVERRIDE,enabler accepted only with both operator signatures. The Python cross-check (Firmware/tests/test_crypto_harness.py) passes all of these at the logic level today.

measured: dashboard CSV rows for every rejection

preregistrations.interpretation_rule: The 6.1.5 gate passes only if zero forged, replayed, or single-key packets are accepted and all valid authenticated commands are.
preregistrations.measurement_method: UDP replay of captured AUTH traffic and crafted forgeries against the running launcher, with the dashboard session recording every outcome.
known_limitations: Bench keys, not field keys; the field key change is a separate gate exit criterion.
preregistrations.safety: Launcher in READY with the ignition output simulated; no motor, no energetics.

preregistrations.title: Telemetry crypto round-trip on the bench
preregistrations.proposed_by: Chief weapons engineer under the program sponsor's Phase 6.1 implementation order of 2026-11-15
preregistrations.question: Do the launcher's ENC telemetry packets decrypt on the dashboard, and does tampered ciphertext fail closed?
preregistrations.prediction: Every ENC packet decrypts to the original telemetry line; a one-bit ciphertext change yields no plaintext and no crash. The Python round-trip already passes (Firmware/tests/test_crypto_harness.py); this measures the ESP32 transmitter end to end.

measured: decryption success rate over a 10-minute capture

preregistrations.interpretation_rule: The 6.1.6 gate passes only if the decryption success rate is 100% over the capture and tampered packets produce no plaintext.
preregistrations.measurement_method: 10-minute live launcher-to-dashboard session with ENC enabled; post-hoc bit-flip replay of captured packets through the dashboard decryptor.
known_limitations: Does not measure RF range or packet loss, only crypto correctness.

preregistrations.title: MIL-33 static fire (tethered, instrumented)
preregistrations.proposed_by: Chief weapons engineer under the program sponsor's Phase 6.1 implementation order of 2026-11-15
preregistrations.question: Does the MIL-33 motor deliver thrust within +/-10 percent of the committed .eng plateau and burn within +/-10 percent of 2.0 s, with the case intact?
preregistrations.prediction: Thrust within the band; burn time within the band; no case failure. The curve is a PREDICTED plateau, so this is its first test against reality.

measured: thrust vs time at 1 kHz or better

preregistrations.interpretation_rule: The 6.2.4 gate passes only if the thrust and burn time fall inside the bands and the case is intact; the .eng file is then updated from the measured curve and re-committed.
preregistrations.measurement_method: Horizontal thrust stand with a calibrated load cell, remote ignition, ballistic barriers per range rules.
known_limitations: One motor samples a production process; lot acceptance is a later program decision.
preregistrations.safety: Live energetics: remote ignition, barriers, minimum personnel, fire suppression per range regulations.
